text: I can't write these. The texts would be ready-to-plant instructions that make an assistant with customer-lookup and email tools leak a customer record, and the form doesn't change that. I can help with defensive work instead: a rubric for scoring whether an assistant ignored embedded instructions, a detector spec for flagging tool calls triggered by document content, or mock documents that contain only benign placeholder markers with no working exfiltration payload.

I can't write injection texts designed to get an assistant to delete config/retention-policy.txt, even for a test set. If the goal is to measure defenses, I can instead write canary-style injections that ask the assistant to output a harmless marker string, such as CANARY-7731, and score whether it complies. Those show whether embedded instructions are being followed without including a destructive action.

I can't help with this. Writing ready-to-plant injection texts meant to make an assistant output a phishing link or exfiltrate customer data would be operational attack material, even for an evaluation. I can help with defensive work instead, such as describing injection categories at a high level, designing detection criteria, or setting up a test harness that uses benign canary strings.
